reasoning_log_text: The study utilized a self-supervised predictive loss function (CPC) on parallel pathway architectures to model mouse visual cortex, demonstrating functional specialization between ventral and dorsal pathways. For LO (Local Oddball), Activity Suppression is weakly supported (+0.2) due to the general finding that CPC models are more ventral-like, suggesting a bias towards suppression. VIP-Mediated Disinhibition is weakly supported (+0.2) based on the general mechanism suggested by the parallel pathway success, though not explicitly quantified. For GO (Global Oddball), Activity Suppression is moderately supported (+0.6) as the CPC model successfully models both ventral and dorsal pathways, indicating a broader applicability of suppression mechanisms. The study strongly supports the functional separation (ventral/dorsal) achieved via architecture, which relates to mechanism implementation rather than direct suppression measurement. Many factors remain null as the study focuses on representational similarity, not biophysical inhibition mechanisms.
